payload.description: Umbrella for closing the gap that a leaked cluster-stored deployer key can stand up operational routes and (today) drain existing routes. Sub-issues cover: moving ISM + warp-route ownership to the hardware wallet, gating the relayer with a curated route whitelist, and minimizing the deploy-time signer. See docs/architecture-decisions.md (deployer authorization) and docs/ops-decisions.md.
payload.title: Harden warp-route deploy authorization & deployer-key custody (SVM bridge)

payload.description:
The core deployer SKIPS the multisig-ISM ownership transfer on a stale assumption. deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh:298-306 says "core transfer-ownership does not exist in the CLI ... Skipping", but `hyperlane-sealevel-client multisig-ism-message-id transfer-ownership --program-id <ism> <new-owner>` DOES exist (verified at the pinned monorepo sha 16c056a, client main.rs:676).

Impact: the ISM access-control owner = deployer key today. multisig-ism-message-id `SetValidatorsAndThreshold` enforces only owner-signer (processor.rs:374-376), so a leaked key can swap in attacker validators and forge messages for EVERY route on that ISM -> drain all collateral. This is the most severe residual hole.

Fix: replace the multisig_ism_message_id "Skipping" branch with a real transfer-ownership to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY, mirroring the working mailbox transfer-ownership block (deploy.sh:289-295). validator_announce has no owner / nothing owner-gated (instruction.rs = Init,Announce only) -> drop its warning, nothing to transfer. No monorepo bump needed (command present at the pin).
payload.title: Transfer multisig-ISM ownership to the hardware wallet during core deploy

payload.description:
warp-deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh transfers only the route programs BPF upgrade authority (solana program set-upgrade-authority, deploy.sh:254-259). The Hyperlane app-level owner is never moved, and build_side (deploy.sh:62-75) sets no owner -> defaults to the deployer key.

Impact: that owner gates enroll_remote_routers / set_interchain_security_module / set_destination_gas / transfer_ownership on each route. A leaked key can re-point a routers or change an existing route ISM and drain that route collateral.

Fix: after deploy + the upgrade-authority transfer, call `hyperlane-sealevel-client token transfer-ownership` (exists at pin, main.rs:346; --token-type Native|Synthetic|Collateral per side, --program-id) to move each side owner to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY. Run LAST, after all owner-gated config (enroll/set-ISM/set-dest-gas) the client does during deploy. Note: once transferred, FORCE_REDEPLOY of an EXISTING route requires the hardware wallet (Ledger) to sign owner ops - acceptable/expected.
payload.title: Transfer warp-route app-level ownership to the hardware wallet during warp deploy

payload.description:
Relayer relays EVERY message between gorchain<->solana: no whitelist set, and HYP_GASPAYMENTENFORCEMENT=[{"type":"none"}] (docker-compose-hyperlane-relayer.yml). Empty MatchingList = relay-all (relayer matching_list.rs:369-375). The mailbox is permissionless (processor.rs dispatch/process), so any deployed route is operational with ZERO operator action; the warp-UI listing is cosmetic.

HYP_WHITELIST is a built-in relayer MatchingList setting (relayer settings mod.rs:50, loaded via the HYP_ env prefix, hyperlane-base loader mod.rs:98) -> config only, no agent code.

Fix: populate HYP_WHITELIST with blessed routes recipient addresses (recipientaddress = H256 hex from each route program-ids.json), assembled in the ops layer from the CURATED git route menu (mirror the warpRoutes.yaml build path), regenerated + relayer restarted when a route is added.

CRITICAL: derive from the curated git source, NOT on-chain discovery - else a leaked-key rogue route auto-whitelists itself and the gate is void. Updating the whitelist is an ops/git-reviewed config change (NOT Ledger): that is the route-endorsement governance gate.
payload.title: Gate the relayer with HYP_WHITELIST built from the curated route menu

payload.description: publish-bridge-state.yml regex-patches deployment-derived scalars (IGP IDs, mailbox, and now HYP_WHITELIST per hyp-d9c.3) into committed specs (spec-relayer.yml/spec-gas-oracle.yml/spec-warp-ui.yml) then commits+pushes. Preferred: derive these on-the-fly from the deployer's generated/ artifacts at deploy time instead of mutating committed specs. Separate concern from hyp-d9c; raised during the authz-hardening design 2026-06-09.
payload.title: Derive prod consumer config from generated artifacts (drop committed-spec patching)
